title: Gate savings behind workload evidence
description: Select a workload and an optimization, then change the evidence window and reliability controls. The gate distinguishes an attractive estimate from a production-ready experiment.
modelNote: Savings rates and policy limits are teaching fixtures. Recalculate them from current prices, demand history, service objectives, and contractual terms before approving a real change.

scenarios.label: Idle non-production cluster
scenarios.detail: The environment is used on weekdays and has no overnight availability objective.

scenarios.label: Steady database baseline
scenarios.detail: A stateful service has predictable year-round demand and a strict latency objective.

scenarios.label: Bursty queue workers
scenarios.detail: Stateless workers can retry jobs, but demand changes sharply during launches.

scenarios.label: Latency-sensitive API
scenarios.detail: The API has uneven peaks and a narrow p99 latency error budget.

actions.label: Schedule off-hours
actions.detail: Stop eligible non-production capacity outside documented working windows.

actions.label: Rightsize capacity
actions.detail: Reduce provisioned capacity and verify service behavior against a control.

actions.label: Purchase commitment
actions.detail: Exchange flexibility for a discounted rate on a measured baseline.

actions.label: Use interruptible capacity
actions.detail: Run restartable work on discounted capacity that the provider may reclaim.
